study.question: Does explicit separation of the inherited same-support and pooled-fallback cases improve use of complementary strict-newer volume, beyond extra columns, shared volume, and provenance indicators alone?
study.hypothesis: Observed r0023 newer-count AUC0.6205084405 beats duplicate0.6204206095 by only0.00008783094 and all-count0.6204044985 by0.00010394197; it worsens Logloss versus r0019 by0.00005537983. These are local single-seed observations, not mechanism confirmation. Probe P=.305419921875 and fallback=.149658203125 imply same=.15576171875 on the first512 only; newer>1 on48.04% of supported coordinates. Current shared count readout conflates algorithm provenance. Explicit signed count interaction may permit different first-layer slopes by provenance without sacrificing the original ordinal/volume representation. This is a falsifiable encoding hypothesis, not an established missing-information bottleneck.

study.proposed_difference: Append8 first-layer columns to the complete r0023 model (all1024 new weights zero, no random draws). Define S=scopes.same_presence, P=burst.gate, Z=2*S-P in{-1,0,1}, c=burst.newer_count. Cells append .5*c*Z, .5*c, .5*Z, or .5*P. Incumbent .5*c retained. Thus common-count plus signed-count can encode separate slopes on S and P\S; indicator cells isolate provenance availability. Both content cells have split/shared magnitude matching; identical parameter count across4 cells. No attention, anchor, age, optimizer or supervision change.
predictions: Primary full-population validation AUC(provenance_count)>AUC(duplicate_count), >AUC(provenance_support) and >incumbent; positive content-by-routing AUC interaction supports conditional volume encoding provisionally.
No systematic Logloss deterioration desired; report its disagreement with primary AUC explicitly, do not change selection criterion.
On S appended routed count equals duplicate count; on P\S sign reverses; outside P all4 values zero. New prefix exactly equals incumbent. Same/fallback reconstruction of c is exact.

Checkpoint probe diagnostics show finite inputs/logits and correct support partition, per-provenance activation, weight/use sensitivity. Checkpoint interventions describe sensitivity only; they are not causal training controls.

Inherited exploratory slices retain sample/positive/negative counts. Do not infer same/fallback performance from category-match-present/absent slices or use first512 to estimate whole-population prevalence.
falsifiers: provenance_count fails to outperform matched duplicate_count and incumbent on primary AUC: this implementation of provenance-volume encoding is unsupported.
provenance_support accounts for gains or interaction<=0: volume-specific attribution unsupported even if a new model wins.
New support is empty, c lacks variation across provenance, or appended features violate partition/prefix/finite checks: implementation/readout hypothesis fails; fix integrity before scores.
Any consequential gain reverses across later paired seeds or user-cluster uncertainty overlaps practical null: keep preliminary or reject robust advantage; no significance from this seed.

AUC interaction is an empirical difference-in-differences, not proof of a user preference mechanism.
